quotes.text: Most people confuse retrieval filters with security boundaries. They are not. Retrieval says search here first. Permissions say you may enter.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up the most common misconception about agent data access.

quotes.text: The thing most people miss is simple. Grounding does not override rights. Grounding filters relevance. It doesn't shrink the agent's legal authority.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why scoping sources alone does not isolate permissions.

quotes.text: The shortcut nobody teaches. Multiple narrow agents beat one encyclopedic monster every time. Build an HR policy agent, a benefits agent, a travel agent, each with their own tight library and enforced filters.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete design recommendation for governable agents.

quotes.text: Yes, you heard that correctly, the user can read it in SharePoint, but the agent gets a no at the processing layer. That's the game changer. Labels plus DLP, decouple human visibility from machine automation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Key insight on separating human access from agent processing.

quotes.text: The truth? Licensing is not a budget line, it's a control surface. With user-based co-pilot, only licensed users can use agent features, which naturally limits sprawl.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes licensing as a governance lever.

Control plane 4: Purview DLP that stops agents

takeaways: Agents see whatever their identity can access through permissions; retrieval filters and grounding only steer relevance, they are not security boundaries.
Scope knowledge sources to single libraries, break inheritance on sensitive libraries and replace broad groups with role-based security groups.
Bind sensitivity labels to Purview DLP policies that block agent processing, and gate agent creation with approvals, licensing controls and data policies.
hook: SharePoint agents don't hallucinate leaks; overscoped sources and permissive inheritance hand them sensitive data at machine speed. This episode is for Microsoft 365 and SharePoint admins rolling out agents. Learn four control planes, from scoping and permissions to approvals and Purview DLP, that cage agents without killing their usefulness.
